theory_sections.content:
The chapter 'Unforgettable Walt Disney' is a biographical sketch written by Roy Disney, Walt's brother. It provides a personal and inspiring look into the life, struggles, and ultimate success of one of the world's greatest animators and storytellers, Walt Disney.

Roy describes Walt as a complex genius—a visionary who was incredibly imaginative, endlessly optimistic, and deeply passionate about his work. To the public, he was a warm, grandfatherly figure, but to those who worked with him, he was a demanding perfectionist.

Walt's journey was not easy. He started with a small animation studio in Kansas City, which ended in bankruptcy. He then moved to Hollywood with just a cardboard suitcase and forty dollars in his pocket.

His first successful creation was 'Oswald the Lucky Rabbit'. However, in a harsh business lesson, his distributor stole the rights to Oswald. Instead of giving up, Walt remained optimistic and declared they would start a new series with a new character: a mouse.

Mickey Mouse was the turning point in Walt Disney's life. Mickey was not just a cartoon character; he was an extension of Walt's own personality.

Walt provided the original squeaky voice for Mickey. The immense success of Mickey Mouse allowed Walt to expand his studio, invest in new technologies, and start producing full-length animated feature films, beginning with 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs'.

Walt had a long-cherished dream of building an amusement park that would be unlike any other in the world—a place where parents and children could have fun together.

For years, he secretly developed plans for Disneyland. When he finally pitched the idea, bankers and critics were highly skeptical, calling it a 'foolish' idea. But Walt persevered. Disneyland opened in 1955 and was a massive success, forever changing the entertainment industry.

Walt Disney was driven by a relentless pursuit of excellence. He believed in constantly improving and 'plussing' his creations. He didn't care much for personal wealth; he poured all his money back into the studio to fund new ideas.

Even on his deathbed, Walt's mind was full of plans for the future (such as the Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow - EPCOT). Roy concludes that Walt's spirit remains alive in the studio and the characters he created, making him truly unforgettable.

definitions.meaning: A person with original ideas about what the future will or could be like.
The state of being completely lacking in a particular quality or value; legally declared inability to pay one's debts.
Persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success.

exercises.question: Who is the author of the chapter 'Unforgettable Walt Disney'?
exercises.explanation: The chapter is a loving tribute written by Walt's brother and business partner, Roy Disney.

exercises.question: What happened to Walt's first successful cartoon character, Oswald the Lucky Rabbit?
options: It became more popular than Mickey Mouse.
Walt sold it for a million dollars.
The distributor stole the rights to the character.
exercises.correct_answer: The distributor stole the rights to the character.
exercises.explanation: Walt lost the rights to Oswald due to a bad contract with his distributor, which forced him to create a new character, Mickey Mouse.

exercises.question: What was Walt's attitude towards money?
options: He hoarded it in secret bank accounts.
He poured it all back into the studio to fund new projects.
He used it to buy luxury yachts and mansions.
exercises.correct_answer: He poured it all back into the studio to fund new projects.
exercises.explanation: Walt was not driven by personal wealth; he saw money purely as a tool to finance his next big creative dream.

previous_year_questions.question: How does Roy Disney describe his brother Walt's personality?
previous_year_questions.answer_hint: He describes him as a complex genius: a warm, grandfatherly figure to the public, but a demanding perfectionist and visionary to those who worked with him.

previous_year_questions.question: What was the reaction of bankers when Walt proposed the idea of Disneyland?
previous_year_questions.answer_hint: They were highly skeptical and considered it a foolish and risky idea.

blocks.title: The Price of Dignity: 20 Cents vs. A Child's Self-Esteem
blocks.title_hi: स्वाभिमान की कीमत: 20 सेंट बनाम बच्चे का आत्म-सम्मान
blocks.title_gu: સ્વાભિમાનની કિંમત: 20 સેન્ટ વિરુદ્ધ બાળકની આત્મ-મર્યાદા
blocks.body: Imagine you are traveling on a bus with a young child. The rule states that children above 1.10 meters must buy a ticket. Your child is just 1 centimeter short. If you don't buy a ticket, you save money that could buy food for days. But your child desperately wants a ticket because to him, buying a ticket means being grown-up, honest, and respected. What would you choose—saving money or preserving a child's pride?
blocks.body_hi: कल्पना कीजिए कि आप एक छोटे बच्चे के साथ बस में यात्रा कर रहे हैं। नियम है कि 1.10 मीटर से अधिक ऊंचाई वाले बच्चों का टिकट लगेगा। आपका बच्चा केवल 1 सेंटीमीटर छोटा है। यदि आप टिकट नहीं खरीदते हैं, तो आप पैसे बचाते हैं जिससे कई दिनों का भोजन आ सकता है। लेकिन आपका बच्चा टिकट खरीदना चाहता है क्योंकि उसके लिए टिकट खरीदने का मतलब है बड़ा होना, ईमानदार होना और सम्मानित होना। आप क्या चुनेंगे—पैसे बचाना या बच्चे के स्वाभिमान की रक्षा करना?
blocks.body_gu: કલ્પના કરો કે તમે એક નાના બાળક સાથે બસમાં મુસાફરી કરી રહ્યા છો. નિયમ છે કે 1.10 મીટરથી વધુ ઊંચાઈ ધરાવતા બાળકોએ ટિકિટ ખરીદવી પડે. તમારું બાળક માત્ર 1 સેન્ટીમીટર નાનું છે. જો તમે ટિકિટ ન ખરીદો તો પૈસા બચે છે. પરંતુ તમારું બાળક ખૂબ જ ઉત્સાહથી ટિકિટ લેવા માંગે છે કારણ કે તેના માટે ટિકિટ ખરીદવી એટલે મોટું થવું, પ્રામાણિક બનવું અને આદર મેળવવો. તમે શું પસંદ કરશો—પૈસા બચાવવા કે બાળકના સ્વાભિમાનનું રક્ષણ કરવું?

blocks.title: A Moral Dilemma on the Bus
blocks.body: When Tao Ying travels alone, she avoids buying a ticket whenever she can save money. However, when she is with her son Xiao Ye, her behavior changes completely. Why does a mother who normally scrimps and saves every penny decide to buy a ticket for a child who doesn't legally need one?
blocks.body_hi: जब ताओ यिंग अकेली यात्रा करती है, तो वह पैसे बचाने के लिए टिकट खरीदने से बचती है। हालाँकि, जब वह अपने बेटे शियाओ ये के साथ होती है, तो उसका व्यवहार पूरी तरह बदल जाता है। सामान्य रूप से एक-एक पैसा बचाने वाली माँ ऐसे बच्चे के लिए टिकट खरीदने का फैसला क्यों करती है जिसे कानूनी रूप से इसकी आवश्यकता नहीं है?
blocks.body_gu: જ્યારે તાઓ યિંગ એકલી મુસાફરી કરે છે, ત્યારે તે પૈસા બચાવવા માટે ટિકિટ ખરીદવાનું ટાળે છે. જો કે, જ્યારે તે તેના પુત્ર શિયાઓ યે સાથે હોય છે, ત્યારે તેનું વર્તન સંપૂર્ણપણે બદલાઈ જાય છે. સામાન્ય રીતે એક-એક પૈસો બચાવતી માતા એવા બાળક માટે ટિકિટ ખરીદવાનું નક્કી શા માટે કરે છે જેને કાયદાકીય રીતે તેની જરૂર નથી?

blocks.title: Understanding the Themes in 'One Centimetre'
blocks.body:
In Bi Shu-min's story 'One Centimetre', we explore three critical themes:

1. Motherhood & Role Modeling: Tao Ying feels an immense responsibility as a mother. She wants to be a perfect, flawless role model for Xiao Ye, even if she feels insignificant in the larger world.
2. Integrity vs. Economy: For a poor family, 20 cents represents real material value (vegetables for days). Yet, moral values and keeping a promise to a child outweigh practical savings.
3. Childhood Dignity: To a child, a ticket is not just travel fare; it is a symbol of identity, truth, and self-worth. Self-esteem bought at twenty cents is a rare and precious investment in childhood.
blocks.body_hi:
बी शू-मिन की कहानी 'वन सेंटीमीटर' में हम तीन महत्वपूर्ण विषयों को समझते हैं:

1. मातृत्व और आदर्श रोल मॉडल: ताओ यिंग एक माँ के रूप में अत्यधिक जिम्मेदारी महसूस करती है। वह शियाओ ये के लिए एक आदर्श माँ बनना चाहती है।
2. ईमानदारी बनाम बचत: एक गरीब परिवार के लिए, 20 सेंट का वास्तविक मूल्य होता है (कई दिनों की सब्जियां)। फिर भी, नैतिक मूल्य और बच्चे से किया गया वादा पैसे की बचत से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण है।
3. बच्चे का आत्म-सम्मान: एक बच्चे के लिए, टिकट केवल किराया नहीं है; यह पहचान और स्वाभिमान का प्रतीक है।
blocks.body_gu:
બી શુ-મિનની વાર્તા 'વન સેન્ટીમીટર' માં આપણે ત્રણ મુખ્ય વિષયો સમજીએ છીએ:

1. માતૃત્વ અને રોલ મોડેલ: તાઓ યિંગ માતા તરીકે ભારે જવાબદારી અનુભવે છે. તે શિયાઓ યે માટે એક સંપૂર્ણ રોલ મોડેલ બનવા માંગે છે.
2. પ્રામાણિકતા વિરુદ્ધ બચત: એક ગરીબ પરિવાર માટે 20 સેન્ટનું વાસ્તવિક મૂલ્ય છે. છતાં, નૈતિક મૂલ્યો અને બાળકને આપેલું વચન આર્થિક બચત કરતાં વધુ મહત્વનું છે.
3. બાળકની આત્મ-મર્યાદા: બાળક માટે ટિકિટ એ માત્ર ભાડું નથી, પરંતુ ઓળખ અને આત્મ-સન્માનનું પ્રતીક છે.

blocks.title: Case Analysis: The Bus Ticket Dilemma
blocks.title_hi: केस विश्लेषण: बस टिकट की दुविधा
blocks.body:
Let us break down Tao Ying's decision-making process into micro-steps:

Step 1: The Context
Tao Ying works hard as a cook and carefully manages her family's meager budget. 20 cents can buy enough spinach for 4 days.

Step 2: The Physical Constraint
The height limit mark on the bus door is 1.10 m. Xiao Ye is exactly 1 centimetre short of reaching this mark.

Step 3: The Child's Conflict
Xiao Ye feels cheated because his mother had promised him a ticket 'next time'. To him, not getting a ticket means he is not tall/big enough and that his mother broke her word.

Step 4: The Decision
Tao Ying decides to buy two tickets despite the conductor pointing out the height rule. She chooses to purchase her son's self-esteem and preserve her promise, prioritizing character building over 20 cents.
blocks.body_hi:
आइए ताओ यिंग के निर्णय लेने की प्रक्रिया का चरणबद्ध विश्लेषण करें:

चरण 1: संदर्भ
ताओ यिंग एक रसोइया के रूप में कड़ी मेहनत करती है और बजट का ध्यान रखती है। 20 सेंट से 4 दिनों की पालक आ सकती है।

चरण 2: शारीरिक सीमा
बस के दरवाजे पर ऊंचाई सीमा 1.10 मीटर है। शियाओ ये इस निशान से ठीक 1 सेंटीमीटर छोटा है।

चरण 3: बच्चे का संघर्ष
शियाओ ये ठगा हुआ महसूस करता है क्योंकि माँ ने 'अगली बार' टिकट दिलाने का वादा किया था। उसके लिए टिकट न मिलना यानी वादा टूटना है।

चरण 4: निर्णय
ताओ यिंग दो टिकट खरीदने का फैसला करती है। वह 20 सेंट की जगह अपने बच्चे के स्वाभिमान और अपने वादे को प्राथमिकता देती है।
blocks.body_gu:
ચાલો તાઓ યિંગના નિર્ણય લેવાની પ્રક્રિયાનું પગલું-દર-પગલું વિશ્લેષણ કરીએ:

પગલું 1: સંદર્ભ
તાઓ યિંગ રસોઈયા તરીકે સખત મહેનત કરે છે. 20 સેન્ટથી 4 દિવસની પાલક ખરીદી શકાય છે.

પગલું 2: ઊંચાઈનો માપદંડ
બસના દરવાજા પર ઊંચાઈની સીમા 1.10 મીટર છે. શિયાઓ યે તેનાથી બરાબર 1 સેન્ટીમીટર નાનો છે.

પગલું 3: બાળકનો સંઘર્ષ
શિઆઓ યે વાયદો તૂટવાથી ગુસ્સે થાય છે. તેના માટે ટિકિટ ન મળવી એ તેના આત્મ-સન્માન પર ચોટ છે.

પગલું 4: નિર્ણય
તાઓ યિંગ બે ટિકિટ ખરીદવાનું નક્કી કરે છે. તે 20 સેન્ટ કરતાં બાળકના આત્મ-સન્માન અને પોતાના વચનને વધુ મહત્વ આપે છે.

blocks.title: Real-World Reflection: What Is Worth More Than Money?
blocks.title_hi: वास्तविक जीवन पर चिंतन: पैसे से अधिक मूल्यवान क्या है?
blocks.title_gu: વાસ્તવિક જીવન પર ચિંતન: પૈસા કરતાં વધુ મૂલ્યવાન શું છે?
blocks.body: In life and commerce, economic calculations often conflict with human values. A short-term financial savings of 20 cents could cause long-term damage to a child's trust and self-esteem. Tao Ying teaches us that true dignity, integrity, and parenting cannot be measured strictly in monetary units.
blocks.body_hi: जीवन और वाणिज्य में, आर्थिक गणनाएँ अक्सर मानवीय मूल्यों से टकराती हैं। 20 सेंट की अल्पकालिक वित्तीय बचत से बच्चे के विश्वास और आत्म-सम्मान को दीर्घकालिक नुकसान हो सकता है। ताओ यिंग हमें सिखाती हैं कि सच्चे स्वाभिमान और चरित्र का मूल्य केवल पैसों से नहीं आंका जा सकता।
blocks.body_gu: જીવન અને વાણિજ્યમાં, આર્થિક ગણતરીઓ ઘણીવાર માનવીય મૂલ્યો સાથે ટકરાય છે. 20 સેન્ટની નાની આર્થિક બચત બાળકના વિશ્વાસ અને આત્મ-સન્માનને મોટું નુકસાન પહોંચાડી શકે છે. તાઓ યિંગ આપણને શીખવે છે કે સાચું સ્વાભિમાન અને નૈતિક મૂલ્ય માત્ર નાણાંથી માપી શકાતા નથી.

blocks.question: Why does Tao Ying buy a bus ticket for Xiao Ye even though he is one centimetre short of the height requirement?
blocks.question_hi: ताओ यिंग शियाओ ये के लिए बस टिकट क्यों खरीदती है, जबकि वह ऊंचाई की आवश्यकता से एक सेंटीमीटर छोटा है?
blocks.question_gu: તાઓ યિંગ શિયાઓ યે માટે બસ ટિકિટ શા માટે ખરીદે છે, જ્યારે તે ઊંચાઈના માપદંડ કરતાં એક સેન્ટીમીટર નાનો છે?
options: She is afraid that the driver will arrest her.
She wants to protect her son's self-esteem and keep her promise to him.
She has plenty of extra money and wants to spend it quickly.
The conductor forced her to buy it under threat of a fine.
options_hi: उसे डर है कि ड्राइवर उसे गिरफ्तार कर लेगा।
वह अपने बेटे के आत्म-सम्मान की रक्षा करना चाहती है और उससे किया वादा निभाना चाहती है।
उसके पास बहुत सारा अतिरिक्त पैसा है और वह इसे जल्दी खर्च करना चाहती है।
कंडक्टर ने उसे जुर्माना लगाने की धमकी देकर खरीदने के लिए मजबूर किया।
options_gu: તેણીને ડર છે કે ડ્રાઇવર તેની ધરપકડ કરશે.
તેણી તેના પુત્રના આત્મ-સન્માનનું રક્ષણ કરવા અને તેને આપેલું વચન પાળવા માંગે છે.
તેની પાસે ઘણા વધારાના પૈસા છે અને તે ઝડપથી ખર્ચવા માંગે છે.
કંડક્ટરે દંડની ધમકી આપીને તેને ખરીદવા મજબૂર કરી.
blocks.explanation: Tao Ying buys the ticket to preserve her child's self-esteem and fulfill her word. To Xiao Ye, having a ticket meant dignity and being treated as an honest person.
blocks.explanation_hi: ताओ यिंग अपने बच्चे के आत्म-सम्मान को बनाए रखने और अपना वादा पूरा करने के लिए टिकट खरीदती है। शियाओ ये के लिए, टिकट होने का मतलब सम्मान और एक ईमानदार व्यक्ति के रूप में माना जाना था।
blocks.explanation_gu: તાઓ યિંગ પોતાના બાળકના આત્મ-સન્માનને જાળવી રાખવા અને પોતાનું વચન પૂરું કરવા માટે ટિકિટ ખરીદે છે. શિયાઓ યે માટે, ટિકિટ હોવાનો અર્થ આદર અને એક પ્રામાણિક વ્યક્તિ તરીકે ગણાવું હતું.
